name: my-dev-team
description: An agentic chat participant for VS Code with tool-calling (read, search, run, write) and built-in feedback.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Triage, oneshot answers, /explain, and the read/search tools work in an untrusted folder; the side-effecting tools (run, write, edit) are disabled and MCP servers are not contacted until you trust the workspace.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Reading, searching, writing, and editing files work in a virtual workspace; the run tool needs a local filesystem and is disabled there.

enumDescriptions: Run the agent pipeline inside the extension against your local Ollama server.

Run the same pipeline in a separate Node process (a sidecar). The tools, approval, and rendering stay in the editor; the engine is isolated. Cloud API keys are read from environment variables, which the child inherits.
Not available yet: will run the same pipeline on a remote backend. Falls back to local with a warning.
myDevTeam.engine.description: Which engine handles @devteam requests. Read live; switching takes effect on the next request.

myDevTeam.model.description: What @devteam uses for the planner, answerer, and executor: a model id, a "provider:<name>" to route among one provider's models (best per task), or "auto" to let the router pick the best available model per agent. The quick triage step is configured separately by myDevTeam.triage.model. Use the /model command or the status-bar item to change it from a list; picking a provider or Auto there sets triage to match in one step.

myDevTeam.triage.model.description: What @devteam uses for the quick internal triage step (deciding whether a request is a question or work). Leave empty to use the build's default (a local Ollama model unless the build changed it). Set it from the /model command's "Triage only" group, or here: "provider:llamacpp" routes to a local llama.cpp server, "provider:openai" (or anthropic/groq) routes within that cloud provider, "auto" picks the best available model, or a model id pins one. A provider or model the build disabled cannot be selected here.

enumDescriptions: Run the quick triage step first, then the answerer or the planner - the default three-agent path.

Run one combined agent that decides the route and produces the answer or the plan in a single call - one fewer round-trip, and a request can never be misrouted into a dead-end answer. Uses your work model (myDevTeam.model), not the triage model.
myDevTeam.triage.mode.description: How @devteam routes a request. Classifier (the default) runs the cheap triage step, then the answerer or planner. Combined runs a single responder that triages and answers-or-plans in one call on your work model. Only the normal path is affected: a slash command (/fix, /plan, ...) still pins the route and uses the dedicated agents.

myDevTeam.complexityRouting.description: Size the executor's model to how demanding triage judges the request: simpler work routes to a cheaper/smaller model, harder work to a stronger one (within whatever provider applies). Turn off to route the executor by capability alone. A pinned model is never affected.

enumDescriptions: Pause for approval only when the planner judges the work complex.
Pause for approval after every drafted plan.
Never pause: run drafted plans straight through (the pre-gate behaviour).
myDevTeam.planApproval.description: When @devteam pauses to let you approve a drafted plan before it runs. At the gate you can Approve (execute), Cancel (keep the plan, run nothing), or Revise (type a comment and have the plan redrafted).

enumDescriptions: Open the preview only for a big plan (complex, or with design decisions, many steps, or a long write-up).
Always open the preview when a plan is paused for approval.
Never open a preview: review the plan inline in the chat only.
myDevTeam.planApproval.preview.description: When a plan paused for approval also opens as a read-only preview in the editor, so you can read the full plan and its design decisions beside the chat. The Approve/Cancel/Revise choices stay in the chat. Only applies when myDevTeam.planApproval pauses for approval.

enumDescriptions: Show everything: triage's detected intent, its reason and complexity; the full plan with each step's detail and the planner's complexity.
Terser output: triage shows only the detected intent; the plan shows its summary and step titles, without per-step details or complexity.
myDevTeam.verbosity.description: How much @devteam shows in the chat. Verbose (the default) shows the agents' full reasoning; Default is a terser view. A pure display choice - it changes nothing the agents do. Switch it with the /verbose command or the My Dev Team status-bar menu.

myDevTeam.attachActiveEditor.description: Automatically attach the file you have open as context on every @devteam request - or just the selected text when you have a selection - so 'analyse the current file' or 'explain this selection' works without attaching anything yourself. On by default. Turn it off to attach nothing automatically (for example to keep a small local model's context window clear, or for privacy); you can still attach files explicitly with the paperclip or #file.

myDevTeam.disabledProviders.description: Providers @devteam must never use (e.g. ["anthropic"]). The router skips their models and the /model picker shows them as disabled, even if an API key is set. A disabled provider never runs even when pinned. This is your personal layer on top of any providers the build itself disables, which you cannot re-enable here.

myDevTeam.disabledModels.description: Individual model ids @devteam must never use (e.g. ["qwen3-coder"]). The router skips them and the /model picker shows them as disabled; a disabled model never runs even when pinned (the run falls back to Auto). On top of any models the build itself disables, which you cannot re-enable here.

id.description: Unique id for this model (must not match a built-in model's id - custom models can only add, not redefine).

label.description: Display name shown in the /model picker and the "which model ran" line.

provider.description: Which already-wired provider hosts the model. New custom models reuse an existing provider's wiring and API key; you cannot add a new provider here.

model.description: The provider-specific model name, e.g. the Anthropic API id (claude-...) or the Ollama tag.

tier.description: The model's weight class for complexity routing. Defaults to "moderate".

capabilities.description: Optional 0-1 capability scores (reasoning, coding, classification, planning, speed, structured-output) used when Auto routes. Optional: a pinned model ignores scores, so you only need these if you want Auto to consider this model.

description.description: Optional one-line note on what the model is good for, shown in the /model picker.

myDevTeam.customModels.description: Extra models to make available without updating the extension, e.g. a newly released Anthropic model. Each entry needs an id, a label, a provider (one already wired: anthropic, openai, google, ollama, llamacpp, groq, deepseek, zai, kimi), and the provider's model name. Cloud models still need that provider's API key. Pin one from the /model picker, or give capability scores to let Auto route to it. Add-only: an entry whose id matches a built-in model is ignored.

myDevTeam.ollama.endpoint.description: Base URL of the Ollama server (origin only, no /api suffix). Leave blank to use the server your deployment ships with, falling back to http://localhost:11434; set a value here to point at your own server (your setting wins over the deployment default). Model calls, error hints, and the startup health check all use the resolved value.

myDevTeam.llamacpp.endpoint.description: Base URL of a local llama.cpp server (llama-server), origin only, no /v1 suffix. Lets @devteam run a small local model without Ollama: install llama-server (llama.cpp), start it with a small model, and point this at its server. Leave blank to use the deployment default, falling back to http://localhost:8080; set a value to point at your own server (your setting wins). To use it for the quick triage step, set myDevTeam.triage.model to "provider:llamacpp".

myDevTeam.openai.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the OpenAI provider (an Azure or OpenAI-compatible gateway). Leave empty to use OpenAI's default endpoint. The API key is read from the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.anthropic.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the Anthropic provider (a proxy or gateway). Leave empty to use Anthropic's default endpoint. The API key is read from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.groq.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the Groq provider (a proxy or gateway). Leave empty to use Groq's default endpoint. The API key is read from the GROQ_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.deepseek.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the DeepSeek provider (a proxy or gateway). Leave empty to use DeepSeek's default endpoint. The API key is read from the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.zai.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the Z.AI provider (the GLM models, a proxy or gateway). Leave empty to use Z.AI's default endpoint (https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4). The API key is read from the ZAI_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.kimi.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the Moonshot Kimi provider (a proxy or gateway). Leave empty to use Kimi's default endpoint (https://api.moonshot.ai/v1). The API key is read from the MOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.google.baseUrl.description: Optional custom base URL for the Google (Gemini) provider (a proxy or gateway). Leave empty to use Google's default Generative Language API endpoint. The API key is read from the GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY environment variable (or, for the local engine, the "Set API Key" command), not here.

myDevTeam.provider.requestsPerMinute.description: Your override for the maximum model requests per minute sent to each provider. Requests are spaced so no provider exceeds this rate, keeping a run under its quota (e.g. a Groq free-tier limit); applied per provider, so a local Ollama call never spends a cloud provider's budget. Leave unset (null) to use the per-provider rate the deployment ships with; set a number to override it (raise or lower), or 0 to disable throttling. A rate-limited (HTTP 429) request is always retried after the delay the provider suggests, regardless of this setting.

myDevTeam.run.commandTimeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds for shell commands started by the run tool. The whole process tree is killed when it expires.

myDevTeam.run.allowedCommands.description: Commands the run tool may execute without an approval prompt, matched as a token-boundary prefix or a glob (e.g. "git status", "npm test", "npm run *"). Only a single, non-chained command matches; a command that chains, pipes, or redirects, or that matches the denylist, always prompts. The Always allow commands like this approval choice appends to this list.

myDevTeam.run.deniedCommands.description: Extra command patterns (same prefix/glob form as run.allowedCommands) that always prompt and are treated as destructive, on top of a non-removable built-in list covering both POSIX commands (rm, git push, git reset, curl, wget, and similar) and the PowerShell equivalents on Windows (Remove-Item, Stop-Process, Invoke-Expression, Format-Volume, and similar). A denylisted command is never auto-approved by an allowlist entry or an existing Allow All grant, regardless of how the agent flagged it.

myDevTeam.read.maxLines.description: Maximum number of lines the read tool returns per call. A partial result names the range shown and the file's total lines so the model can continue.

myDevTeam.search.globMaxResults.description: Maximum number of files a glob search returns.

myDevTeam.search.contentScanLimit.description: Maximum number of files a content search scans.

myDevTeam.search.contentMaxMatches.description: Maximum number of matches a content search collects before stopping early.

myDevTeam.chat.toolSnippetLines.description: Number of leading lines of a written file's contents shown as a snippet under the write call in the execution transcript. 0 hides the snippet.

myDevTeam.executor.checkpointEverySteps.description: During a long task, @devteam pauses after this many tool-calling steps and asks whether to keep going or stop and summarize what it has so far. 0 turns the step-based check-in off. Whichever of this and myDevTeam.executor.checkpointEverySeconds is reached first triggers the check-in.

myDevTeam.executor.checkpointEverySecond.description: During a long task, @devteam pauses after this many seconds and asks whether to keep going or stop and summarize what it has so far. 0 turns the time-based check-in off. Whichever of this and myDevTeam.executor.checkpointEverySteps is reached first triggers the check-in.

myDevTeam.executor.contextWarnThresholds.description: Context-usage levels (as a percentage of the model's context window) at which @devteam shows a notice during a long run, so you can tell when it is close to filling the model's window. Each level below myDevTeam.history.autoCompactThreshold also offers a "Compact now" action; at or above the threshold the conversation auto-compacts instead (when myDevTeam.history.autoCompact is on). Each level warns once. An empty list falls back to the default.

myDevTeam.history.autoCompact.description: Automatically compact the conversation when its context nears the model's window. Once a run crosses myDevTeam.history.autoCompactThreshold, your next message first summarizes the conversation so far and continues against that summary, so a long session cannot silently overflow the window. Turn off to only ever compact when you click the "Compact now" action the warnings offer (or run /compact).

myDevTeam.history.autoCompactThreshold.description: Context-usage level (as a percentage of the model's context window) at or above which the conversation auto-compacts on your next message (when myDevTeam.history.autoCompact is on). Below it, a context warning only offers a manual "Compact now" action. Set it to one of myDevTeam.executor.contextWarnThresholds for the trigger to line up with a warning.

myDevTeam.modelContextWindows.description: Per-model context-window sizes in tokens, keyed by model id (e.g. {"qwen3-coder": 32768}). Overrides the built-in value, which matters most for local models: their real window is whatever the server was started with (num_ctx), not the model's theoretical maximum. Used only to calculate the context-usage warnings.

myDevTeam.instructions.files.description: Project instruction files probed in the workspace root, in order; the first one found is given to the agents as standing instructions on every request. Plain file names only (no folders). An empty list turns the feature off.

myDevTeam.skills.directories.description: Root-relative directories scanned for skills, each at <dir>/<name>/SKILL.md. A skill is a named, described block of instructions the agent loads on demand when a task matches its description (built-in skills ship with the extension regardless). An empty list turns workspace skills off; an entry that is absolute or contains .. makes the whole list fall back to the default.

command.description: The executable to launch the MCP server (e.g. "npx").

env.description: Environment variables for the server process.

myDevTeam.mcp.servers.markdownDescription: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers whose tools @devteam may call, as a name -> definition map, e.g. `{ "filesystem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."] } }`. Each server is launched over stdio; its tools are offered to the model namespaced as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, and every call is approved through the same prompt the run tool uses. Server names must be plain identifiers (letters, digits, _ , -); invalid entries are ignored. No server is contacted in an untrusted workspace. New or changed servers take effect on a window reload.

myDevTeam.write.protectedPaths.description: Root-relative locations the write and edit tools refuse to touch, on top of the always-protected .git/ (these can run code automatically, e.g. VS Code tasks). Matched per path segment, so .git does not catch .gitignore. An empty list keeps only .git protected; an entry with .. makes the whole list fall back to the default.

myDevTeam.approval.fileChanges.description: Require approval before the write and edit tools change a file. Off by default: changes apply immediately, since a git-backed workspace makes them recoverable. Turn this on to confirm every write and edit with the same Approve/Decline prompt the run tool uses (the run tool is always gated, regardless of this setting). Read live; takes effect on the next request.

myDevTeam.usage.showInChat.description: Append a Tokens line under each reply summing the run's input and output tokens. The status-bar session total and the My Dev Team: Show Token Usage report are independent of this setting.

myDevTeam.changes.showInChat.description: Append a Changes line under a reply that wrote files, summing them as "N files changed, +X -Y". The line only appears when a turn actually changed files.

myDevTeam.summary.showInChat.description: After an executed plan that changed files, add a Summary recap in three sections (What ships, How it's built, Tests and docs). Turning this off skips the extra summarizer model call entirely.

myDevTeam.thinking.showInChat.description: Capture a reasoning model's thinking while it works. The live "is reasoning" indicator is VS Code's own built-in progress (the rotating "Thinking"/"Generating"/… verbs), shown either way; this only controls capturing the reasoning so its duration can be timed. Turning it off skips capturing entirely (and removes the "Thought for Ns" line).

myDevTeam.thinking.showDuration.description: After a reasoning model finishes, append a "Thought for Ns" line under the reply showing how long it spent thinking. Requires myDevTeam.thinking.showInChat (the time is measured from the thinking it surfaces).

myDevTeam.clarify.enabled.description: Let @devteam ask you a clarifying question instead of guessing when a request is genuinely ambiguous. The run ends with one or more questions (each with suggested answers you can click, or you can type your own); your reply on the next turn carries the work forward. Turn this off to make @devteam always pick a sensible assumption and proceed without asking.

myDevTeam.telemetry.evalLog.description: Store a local eval log of @devteam runs (route, per-step model and token usage, outcome) and thumbs up/down feedback as JSON lines in the extension's global storage. No prompts, file contents, or replies are recorded, and nothing leaves your machine. The My Dev Team: Show Token Usage report reads this log.

myDevTeam.telemetry.shadowTriage.description: On a slash-command run (which pins the route), also run triage in the background to record what it would have decided, so the Show Token Usage report can score triage against the command you chose. Adds one local triage call per pinned run and only collects data while the eval log is on. Off by default.

myDevTeam.debug.description: Log all communication between the chat client, the engine backend (the in-process or sidecar engine), and the AI provider's API - including the raw request and response messages - to the "My Dev Team (Debug)" output channel. Off by default. Turn it on only to diagnose a problem: the log is verbose and the raw messages contain your prompts, file contents, and the model's replies. Everything stays on your machine.

commands.name: ask
commands.description: Ask a quick side question - answered directly, never joins the conversation.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Start fresh: drop the conversation so far from future requests.

commands.name: model
commands.description: Choose the model for the whole team or a single agent (or Auto to route by capability).

commands.name: verbose
commands.description: Choose how much @devteam shows in the chat: verbose (everything) or default (terser).

commands.name: compact
commands.description: Summarize the conversation so far; the summary then stands in for it.

commands.name: do
commands.description: Plan and execute workspace changes - no triage.

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain a file, selection, or concept in the chat - no changes made.

commands.name: fix
commands.description: Diagnose a bug, fix its root cause, and verify the fix.

commands.name: plan
commands.description: Draft the step-by-step plan but do not execute it.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review the attached code or selection - findings in chat, no edits.

commands.name: test
commands.description: Write or update tests for the target code, then run them.
